cvEn:
Avraham Mula, son of Jacklin and Ezra, was born on the 15th of Heshvan 5724 (2 November 1963) in the city of Jaffa. Avraham was the eldest in a large family, with nine siblings: Miri, Itzik, Kobi, Shlomi, Rafi, Eli, Avihai (Avraham Chai), and the twins Shimon and Bruria.

Avraham grew up and was educated at the Weizmann Elementary School in Jaffa. He then attended the Ironi Gimel High School in Jaffa, where he completed his studies in the biology track with outstanding distinction. He was very much loved by the entire educational staff, a special child. He was an example and a role model at home, among his close friends, and in the IDF. He always liked to help his parents at home with his younger siblings. In his free time he liked to contribute to society and volunteered for a lonely elderly person, which brought him great satisfaction.

In January 1982 he enlisted in the IDF and served in the Armored Corps as a tank crewman. After a few months he was assigned to the 77th Battalion ("Oz") of the 7th Brigade.

During his training he specialized as a tank driver. His fellow soldiers and commanders in the battalion testified to his great professionalism, outstanding achievement, dedication, and the good spirit he brought to his crew and to the battalion.

During Operation Peace for Galilee he served with his battalion in the Beqaa Valley in Lebanon. On 10 September 1982, Avraham was on a patrol in a tank in the Jebel Barouk area. He was ambushed by terrorists and killed.

Private Avraham Mula fell in battle in Lebanon during Operation Peace for Galilee on the 22nd of Elul 5742 (10 September 1982). He was nineteen years old when he fell. He was buried in the Holon Military Cemetery. He left behind parents and siblings. After his death he was promoted to Corporal.

About two months after his death, his mother Jacklin gave birth to a brother, who was named after him: Avihai (Avraham Chai).

Defense Minister Ariel Sharon wrote to his family: "Corporal Avraham Mula fell in the Beqaa Valley in a clash with an ambush of terrorists. Avraham was a reliable soldier, full of motivation, quiet and calm, always with a smile on his lips."

His unit commander wrote about him: "Avraham was a tank driver and performed his role in the best possible way. He was a quiet and calm young man, always smiling. He was very attached to his home, and he spoke about this connection with his friends."

A reading corner of holy books was established in his name at the synagogue in Neve Ofer, where his family prays.

His loved ones created a Facebook page in his memory called: "In memory of my father Mula, may he rest in peace."
